summary: The branch implements the agreed phrase segmentation, Groq whisper-large-v3 selection, omission of language and prompt, ordered insertion into both targets, failure markers, and API cancellation on Quick Idea close; index.html and voice.html are unchanged. The tests meaningfully exercise these behaviors, and node tests/verify.js passes. However, Web Audio startup failures can leak an acquired microphone stream with no working Stop control, which blocks merge. A Node harness reproduced this against the actual module: throwing from createMediaStreamSource rejected toggleDictation, and even stopDictation(target, {discard:true}) left zero tracks stopped and zero contexts closed. Independent Playwright validation was blocked: all 31 tests failed before assertions because Chromium startup hit sandbox_host_linux.cc:41, Operation not permitted; this does not contradict the tester's reported earlier 31/31 pass. Real Groq mixed-language recognition remains unverified, as acknowledged by both reports, and still needs the spec section 12 check.
findings: [P2] js/markdown/dictation.js:276-291: Protect the complete Web Audio startup after getUserMedia succeeds. AudioContext construction, createMediaStreamSource, createScriptProcessor, and connect can throw, and ctx.resume() can reject. Currently the stream/context remain local until line 289, so a failure before that assignment leaves the microphone running, the button inactive, and stopDictation unable to release it; the exception also escapes without a user-facing failure. Add cleanup for every partially acquired resource, remove or avoid registering the unfinished session, handle resume rejection, and report startup failure through the existing localized error path. Add regressions for a thrown setup operation and rejected resume that assert tracks stop, any created context closes, no recorder remains active, and a subsequent start succeeds.
